core_struggle: A student under twenty-five with a restless mind and seven hours of phone time, who feels stressed but cannot say why.
mirror: You lie awake with a mind that will not settle, and the phone is the last thing you reach for.

queries.hook: A mind that will not settle, running on its own, and the phone that keeps it running.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy and will not rest.
queries.steady: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong; holding it feels like holding the wind, but it can be stilled.
queries.act: Practise steadying the mind through one breath, one task, one moment at a time, and let the phone wait.
queries.story: A young student whose mind would not settle, who took up a practice and found that the wind can be stilled.

bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
week_thesis: Seven days from a mind that will not settle to one quiet minute a day where the wind stops.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the restlessness and the phone as one thing, not two.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the mind runs on its own and becomes its own enemy when left to itself.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the mind can be stilled, even if it feels like the wind now.
week_beats.act: You try one quiet minute before the phone, one task done fully, and one breath taken slowly.
week_beats.story: A young student who could not settle, who took up a practice and found that the wind can be stilled.

insight: You are stressed and you cannot say why. The truth is that the mind has been running on its own for too long.
seat: a student whose mind will not settle and whose phone takes up most of the day
life_context: A student under twenty-five, studying and staring at the phone for hours, with a mind that will not settle; the stress is there but the cause is not yet named.
details: daily phone time is seven hours
